metadata.title: Focused forward-citation chain resolution for 2025 records outside the database union
metadata.scope: The 16 year-2025 focused-scope forward-chain candidates in research/citation_chaining.json that had no exact normalized DOI or normalized-title match in research/search_union_deduplicated.json.
metadata.deduplication: Exact normalized DOI first; whitespace/punctuation/case-normalized title second. Parent seed IDs and discovery sources are preserved verbatim from citation_chaining.json.
metadata.eligibility_rule: Core records computationally perform, evaluate, or directly support qualitative coding/thematic interpretation. Adjacent records empirically study validity, representation, researcher practice, or governance that changes how such systems should be evaluated. Topic modelling alone and protocols without completed evidence are excluded.
metadata.version_family_note: The COREQ+LLM preprint DOI 10.2196/preprints.78682 and journal-protocol DOI 10.2196/78682 are two records for one protocol family; both are preserved below and excluded for the same prospective-design reason.

records.title: When LLMs Fall Short in Deductive Coding: Model Comparisons and Human–AI Collaboration Workflow Design
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: Compares transformer classifiers and LLMs on two imbalanced dialogue-coding datasets and evaluates a human–AI escalation workflow; the abstract reports systematic LLM errors and an indispensable human role.
records.eligibility_reason: Direct empirical evaluation of deductive qualitative dialogue coding and a human–AI adjudication workflow.
records.full_text_reason: The inspected paper reports two coded educational-dialogue datasets, nine model variants, rare-code analysis, human adjudication, and comparative reliability/efficiency results. It is an arXiv v1 preprint submitted 24 December 2025; its statement that it was prepared for LAK 2026 is not treated as verified peer review.

records.title: Understanding Graduate School Through AI: A Scalable Approach to Thematic Coding
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: Uses human grounded coding to construct a codebook and GPT-4 Turbo to apply binary sentence-level codes across 89 graduate-student interviews.
records.eligibility_reason: Direct human-guided computational thematic coding of a substantial qualitative interview corpus.

retrieval.note: The terminal PDF endpoint returned an access error, but the complete official article text was available and inspected through the publisher rendering.

records.full_text_reason: The inspected article reports 89 interviews and more than 18,000 sentences, a human-derived codebook, temperature-zero GPT-4 Turbo binary classification, manual validation, and downstream statistical analyses.

records.title: Simulacrum of Stories: Examining Large Language Models as Qualitative Research Participants
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: An interview-and-probe study of 19 qualitative researchers examines representational, epistemic, consent, agency, positionality, and erasure risks when LLMs substitute for research participants.
records.eligibility_reason: LLMs are participant proxies rather than analysts, but the empirical validity and ethics findings directly constrain computational qualitative-analysis evaluation.
records.full_text_reason: The inspected CHI paper empirically establishes six distinct limitations of synthetic participant data and reports its own reflexive thematic-analysis procedure, IRB approval, and privacy-based nonrelease decision.

records.title: Proof of Concept: Leveraging Large Language Models for Qualitative Analysis of Participant Feedback
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: Compares human inductive/focused coding with ChatGPT 3.5 coding of Extension-program participant feedback and reports complementary strengths plus need for oversight.
records.eligibility_reason: Direct empirical comparison of human and LLM qualitative coding.

retrieval.source: official Journal of Extension repository PDF

records.full_text_reason: The inspected article reports 118 participants, three human coders, an explicit human/ChatGPT protocol, five final human codes, κ=.392, 60% focused-code matching, and an approximately 15-minute AI run versus weeks of human work.

records.title: LOGOS: LLM-driven End-to-End Grounded Theory Development and Schema Induction for Qualitative Research
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: Introduces an end-to-end automated grounded-theory/schema-induction pipeline with coding, clustering, graph reasoning, iterative refinement, a five-dimensional metric, train/test evaluation, and five corpora.
records.eligibility_reason: Direct system and evaluation contribution for inductive coding and theory/schema development.
records.full_text_reason: The inspected preprint reports an auditable multi-stage pipeline, five datasets and six baselines, metric validation with two authors, repeated refinement results, and a manual schema-alignment check; the 88.2% figure uses a permissive any-match rule and is not precision.

records.title: LLM-Assisted Automated Deductive Coding of Dialogue Data: Leveraging Dialogue-Specific Characteristics to Enhance Contextual Understanding
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: Evaluates separate event/act prompts, three LLM families, an equal-weight ensemble, and GPT-4o consistency checking for deductive coding of collaborative-learning dialogue.
records.eligibility_reason: Direct computational deductive-coding system with human-coded reference data and multiple reliability metrics.
records.full_text_reason: The inspected AIED paper reports 5,676 utterances from 24 participants, two-human reference coding, train/validation/test partitions, three model families with five runs each, ensemble and contextual-consistency ablations, and model–human reliability below human–human reliability.

records.title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Thematic Analysis: A Case Study in the Charity Sector
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: Uses three Tearfund datasets to evaluate GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini as initial annotator and validator in deductive and inductive thematic coding.
records.eligibility_reason: Direct real-world LLM-assisted thematic-coding evaluation with human comparators.

retrieval.source: White Rose Research Online open-access version of record

records.full_text_reason: The inspected article reports codebook-specific κ, sentiment and evidence-of-impact failures, inductive cosine similarity, extraction precision/recall, variability, staff feedback, reusable prompts, and the time cost of human validation. It was accepted and published online in 2025; the issue year is 2026.

records.title: LATA: A Pilot Study on LLM-Assisted Thematic Analysis of Online Social Network Data Generation Experiences
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: The official abstract describes Braun-and-Clarke-style inductive thematic analysis of 14 researcher interviews, followed by GPT-4 and Gemini analysis and semantic comparison up to cosine similarity .76.
records.eligibility_reason: The abstract is a clear direct fit, but methodological extraction requires the complete article.

retrieval.source: ACM DOI landing page and official abstract only
failed_routes: ACM PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403; no reproducibly accessible author manuscript was located

records.full_text_reason: Do not convert nonretrieval to exclusion. Retain as a core full-text candidate; no 52-field extraction or quality score was created.

records.title: Large Language Models in Qualitative Research: Uses, Tensions, and Intentions
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: Interviews 20 qualitative researchers about actual and imagined LLM uses, nonuse, privacy, agency, methodological norms, and interpretive tensions.
records.eligibility_reason: Empirical researcher-practice and governance evidence directly informs human-role and validity requirements, although it does not benchmark a coding system.

retrieval.source: University of Michigan Deep Blue author manuscript

records.full_text_reason: The inspected CHI paper reports 20 interviews, an inductive thematic analysis, IRB approval, and detailed findings on privacy, interpretive intimacy, skill gaps, intentional tool design, and risks of methodological slippage.

records.title: From Transformers Come Themes: Evaluating BERTopic for Qualitative Analysis of Social Media Data
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: Operationalizes the claimed qualitative analysis as an enhanced BERTopic topic-modeling pipeline evaluated with topic quality, coherence, precision, recall, and F-score.
records.eligibility_reason: Exclude under the explicit topic-modeling criterion: no qualitative code/theme interpretation or directly relevant evaluation contribution beyond BERTopic clustering is established.

records.title: Extension of the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research Guideline to Large Language Models (COREQ+LLM): Protocol for a Multiphase Study (Preprint)
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: Prospectively specifies four phases to develop and validate a reporting extension; no completed guideline or validation results are reported.
records.eligibility_reason: Exclude protocol under the stated criterion. This preprint is the same study family as FC25-012 and contributes no completed empirical or methodological foundation at the cutoff.

records.title: Extension of the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research Guideline to Large Language Models (COREQ+LLM): Protocol for a Multiphase Study
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: The published JMIR record remains a prospective protocol for guideline development and validation rather than a completed reporting guideline.
records.eligibility_reason: Exclude protocol under the stated criterion. This is the journal version of FC25-011, so counting it as a separate study would also duplicate the same protocol family.

records.title: Exploring Differences Between Hybrid GPT-Human and Human-Created Qualitative Codebooks in an Educational Game
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: Compares a GPT-4-plus-human codebook against a fully human codebook on middle-school WHIMC observations, including human reliability and external-criterion/ENA analyses.
records.eligibility_reason: Direct comparison of human and hybrid LLM–human qualitative codebook development.
records.full_text_reason: The inspected ICQE paper reports independent human and hybrid codebook construction, blinded human codebook application, κ results, automated coding, conceptual overlap, and external interest/ENA comparisons; hybrid codes were broader while human codes retained finer distinctions.

records.title: Collaborative AI for Qualitative Analysis: Bridging AI and Human Expertise for Scalable Analysis
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: Introduces CAILA, a GPT-4o thematic-analysis tool with an explicit saturation stopping rule, and compares human+CAILA analysis with two-human analysis on 146 utterances.
records.eligibility_reason: Direct system and human-comparator study of iterative thematic analysis.
records.full_text_reason: The inspected workshop paper reports 146 student-conversation utterances, ten CAILA iterations, a three-no-new-themes saturation rule, comparison with two human researchers, and a key limitation: humans refined the research question while the AI remained bound to it.

records.title: Code-Aware LLM Prompting in Deductive Qualitative Analysis: A Study in Multi-framework Analysis of Learning Designs
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: Compares uniform and code-specific adaptive prompting for Llama 3.3 70B against two expert coders over 35 learning designs, 758 items, 13 codes, and three pedagogical frameworks.
records.eligibility_reason: Direct deductive qualitative-coding evaluation with human reference coding, repeated runs, reliability metrics, and public artifacts.

retrieval.source: indexed author manuscript plus official Zenodo research package
retrieval.note: The publisher chapter was not openly downloadable; the complete indexed manuscript text and the authors' codebook, dataset, prompts, coding outputs, and agreement report were inspected.

records.full_text_reason: The inspected paper/package reports code-aware expert- and data-driven prompt rules, three runs per code, Gwet AC1 and κ under label imbalance, token use, two expert coders, and openly deposited prompts/data/coding outputs.

records.title: Auto-Coding Collaborative Dialogue from Classrooms with Open LLMs Using Zero-Short Prompting
records.outside_union_check: no exact normalized DOI or title match
records.abstract_evidence: Evaluates self-prompting, chain-of-thought, and in-context zero-shot strategies with open LLMs for inductive coding of classroom collaborative dialogue, plus an expert five-dimension code-quality rubric.
records.eligibility_reason: Direct evaluation of open-model qualitative coding and prompt strategies on authentic dialogue.
records.full_text_reason: The inspected proceedings paper reports more than 210,000 words from 38 student dyads, open Llama/Qwen models, three prompting strategies, an expert rubric, and failure patterns including low recall and theoretical drift.
